Subject: Velotech pilot — runway top-up framework and conversion path

Hi Sara / Tom,

Great demo last week — thanks again for walking through the retrieval/agent flows. Per our conversation, I pulled together two pragmatic ways to give the team more runway while keeping the evaluation aligned to production economics:

1) Short extension + conversion credit: add 14 days to the current timebox and provide a one-time pilot credit equal to 20% of the committed trial spend. If you convert to a paid Dedicated/Hosted contract within 60 days after the extended pilot we apply the credit to the first invoice.

2) Top-up hours (burst bucket): provide a one-off bucket of 200 GPU-hours at a preferential pilot rate (10% off list) that you can draw from during the existing pilot window. Unused hours cannot be converted to dollars but can be applied as a discount within 30 days.

Attached is a short two-page proposal with both options (velotech_proposal_v1.pdf). Quick ask: which option looks closest to what you need? If helpful I can carve a hybrid (7-day extension + 100-hour top-up) — happy to run numbers.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Wednesday to lock this down? Calendar link: https://cal.redwood.ai/jordan/30

Best,

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the options. A couple quick clarifying questions before we sync: 

- For option 1, does the 20% pilot credit apply to the total pilot spend or only to incremental spend during the extension? We need something that translates cleanly to our finance team.
- For option 2, can the unused hours be rolled into a first-month discount if we decide to move to Dedicated? The legal team prefers credits-to-invoice if possible.

Also, what flexibility do you have on % for the credit? Our pilot had some unexpected latency work, so the team is asking if you can stretch to 25% on option 1, or alternatively a smaller extension (7 days) with 25% credit.

I can do Wed 11am PT if that works.

Marissa / team — quick finance read: 

We can approve a conversion-linked pilot credit up to 25% on the *incremental* spend of the extension (not the entire pilot) without executive sign-off, provided we attach a conversion clause (convert to a MRR/commit within 60 days of the extension end) and include a clawback if they churn within 90 days. If the customer wants the credit applied to the *first invoice* dollar-for-dollar, legal will need to confirm language but that's typical.

Alternate option: approve a 14-day extension + 20% credit on the incremental extension spend as a faster internal approval path. If you want to land on 25% across the board, request needs to go to revenue ops for final sign-off — I'll prepare a short memo.

I've attached a one-page approval memo draft (finance_approval_memo.pdf) with the incremental-credit math and recommended clawback language.

-David

Sara / Tom — thanks for the quick response and for surfacing the finance preference. Based on internal alignment here are two clean, actionable offers we can bring to the Wed call: 

A) 14-day extension + 20% conversion credit on incremental extension spend. Credit applies to first invoice if the account converts within 60 days of the extension end. Standard 90-day clawback applies if the account cancels within that window. (This is our quick-approve path.)

B) Hybrid: 7-day extension + 100-hour top-up at 25% credit (applied against incremental pilot spend and convertible to invoice credit upon conversion within 60 days). This option is slightly more aggressive on credit but limits total exposure.

If either looks good I will:
- Send an updated two-page proposal (I attached velotech_proposal_v1 - updated.pdf)
- Open a HubSpot record update (HS-482719) and route the DocuSign template for the conversion clause if you sign off on A.

Can we lock on option A or B on Wed 11am PT? If yes I will share the proposal before the call.

Next steps: Wed 11am PT call; Jordan to send updated proposal; Velotech to confirm preferred option.
